nodes.label: ADR 0013: Index population gate stays on dictionary query
nodes.rationale: Alembic startup readiness only guarantees canonical schema. Whether Bosworth-Toller lookup tables have rows is a separate gate so an empty database after migrate stays valid for dictionary build and invalid for dictionary query. The gate is a query-module function rather than BTQueryService policy because construction already preloads the normalized-title index and morphology generation constructs BTQueryService when dictionary rows may be empty.

nodes.label: Index population gate
nodes.rationale: The gate counts BTEntry, BTSense, and BTVariant rows on a short-lived SQLAlchemy connection and treats a missing SQLite table as count zero. A missing file raises FileNotFoundError and must not create a database. Other SQLAlchemy failures propagate. The CLI formats ClickException with the path, table names, and wyrdcraeft dictionary build; the domain type does not own that sentence. Empty tables stay valid for dictionary build.

nodes.label: Alembic startup schema readiness (ADR 0002)
nodes.rationale: Startup Alembic readiness only guarantees the canonical schema. Folding row-population into that check would block empty-database dictionary builds, so population stays a separate query-module gate.

nodes.label: BTQueryService
nodes.rationale: The population gate is not a BTQueryService method and not constructor policy. __init__ already preloads the normalized-title index, and generation constructs the service when dictionary rows may be empty. Putting the gate in __init__ or in db.runtime would block those callers or couple population to schema readiness.

nodes.label: Morphology generation-runner path resolver
nodes.rationale: Default morphology input paths stay on the generation-runner resolver, exported so generate-reference-snapshots does not duplicate them. dictionary build still passes path overrides into that runner.

hyperedges.label: Schema readiness, query population, and browse readiness are separate checks
